messages:
mara: Heads up — proposing a week-long soft-redirect for /v1/text.generate -> /v2/text.generate on a per-route basis next Tue. Want to surface costs/compat risk in the console before we flip.
jonathan: +1. do we have a clear plan for quota attribution when we route a v1 token to v2? billing team will ask.
ash: We currently attribute to the receiving model route. That makes charged unit and telemetry reflect v2, which hides the "origin" in billing.
sam: That causes two problems: customers see bill change with no obvious trace, and our migration metrics undercount v1->v2 redirects.
anna-ux: UX ask — console needs a preview: per-route "expected bill delta" and a heatmap showing tenants with high compatibility risk. Non-technical PMs should be able to see impact in dollars.
mara: Agreed. Proposal: add an attribution tag on token events when we do server-side routing: `origin_version=v1` and `routed_version=v2`. That way billing + telemetry can split by origin or routed.
jonathan: That fixes accounting. But we'll also need to expose it in the per-tenant quota/cost table and in the rollouts dashboard; otherwise ops will be blind.
nash: Implementation detail: augment request pipeline to inject `X-Redwood-Origin-Version: v1` header preserved across proxies and into usage pings. Billing ingestion picks that up as `origin_version`.
sam: Are there privacy/security implications? Headers get into logs/audit. We should gate retention. Also add opt-out via tenant setting.
mara: Good point — add retention TTL and an enterprise opt-out toggle. For the console preview we can run a dry-run over the last 7 days using current traffic and compute projected token delta if routed to v2 (token_count * ratio_v2_token_increase).
anna-ux: UI sketch: small modal on route page, "Preview auto-route to v2" -> shows 7d baseline tokens, estimated tokens on v2, estimated $ delta, list of top impacted tenants with quick links. Also a small "compatibility score" (0–100) based on eval set failures and error spike risk.
jonathan: Operationally, rollout plan suggestion: 0% shadow -> 1% canary -> 10% canary -> 50% -> 100%, with automatic rollback if: latency + p95 increases >25% OR token_per_request increases >30% OR error_rate increases >0.5% absolute.
nash: Need telemetry for silent upgrades too: count of requests that had `origin_version` != `routed_version`. Add metric `compat.silent_routed_count` tagged by route/tenant.
sam: Also add a console metric that correlates silent_routed_count with `billing_delta_estimate`. That helps finance and support.
mara: For the deploy bot: after each canary step, post a short summary: canary_start, sample_size, metric_deltas, top-tenant-deltas, and whether rollback triggered.
deploy-bot: (system) canary job queued: `canary-run 1767777778` — will post results to thread once complete.
anna-ux: Copy for customer banner: "We're upgrading your gen endpoint for better latency and cheaper inference. Preview expected bill impact in Console -> Routes." Keep it simple.
jonathan: One edge: older SDK clients that pin `version=v1` may expect older behavior. We should make default routing only for requests WITHOUT explicit `version` header, and for requests that include `prefer_version=v1` we must respect it.
nash: Implementation: routing precedence: 1) explicit `prefer_version` header 2) console pin overrides 3) automatic routing policy. We'll map that into router config and unit tests.
mara: Actions: (1) infra to emit `origin_version` header and metrics (owner: jonathan) (2) billing pipeline to consume `origin_version` and show preview (owner: sam) (3) UX mock for preview modal and heatmap (owner: anna-ux) (4) deploy-bot canary messages update (owner: infra) — aim to have a dry-run preview by EOD Fri.
sam: I'll sync with billing; putting tentative ETA on the ticket.
anna-ux: I'll drop a quick Figma link later.
jonathan: I can kick off a small internal runbook for rollback steps once we have metrics emitted.
mara: Thanks all. If anyone has objections to the attribution tag plan, call it out now. Otherwise I'll file the rollout PR and the console spec.
nash: No objections from me.
sam: SGTM.
deploy-bot: (system) scheduled: canary-run 1767777778 at 1767777900
